name: Tonga
summary: Tonga allows wills, and intestacy gives a widow one third and children two thirds, but no fixed share was found for a will. Land is hereditary and mostly cannot be sold to foreigners. Trust and foundation law and the Hague Trusts Convention were not confirmed.
family_claims: No general family-provision statute found (only the Maintenance of Deserted Wives Act). A widow has a customary right to the family house on the town allotment.
foreign_law_note: No conflict-of-law rule was sourced. English Wills Act 1837 and Administration of Estates Act 1925 apply as received law.
trust_note: Trust law is received English law; no trust tax regime or Tongan trust statute was sourced, so 'limited' is recorded pending confirmation. No foundation law was found.
open_questions: Whether a Tongan Trustee or trust statute exists.
Probate Act (Cap 16) text, and treatment of royal estates and noble titles.
